husk.name: PANDA COCOfiber
husk.imageAlt: Golden high-tensile coconut coir fibers decorticated with electric machinery
husk.description: The tough outer husk yields resilient, golden fibers naturally rich in lignin. Mechanically extracted via electric decorticators without harsh chemicals, yielding rot-resistant industrial grade fibers.
husk.p1: High natural lignin content (~45%) resists microbial rot and moisture
husk.p2: Exceptional tensile strength and natural elasticity for manufacturing
husk.p3: 100% renewable substitute for fossil-based synthetic fibers and foams
husk.gain: Replaces petroleum-based polymers in orthopedic mattresses, automotive seating, and erosion-control geotextiles.

pith.name: PANDA COCOpeat
pith.imageAlt: Organic porous cocopeat certified Low-EC for commercial horticulture nurseries
pith.description: Held between long fibers is a spongy cellular pith with remarkable moisture-holding capacity. Through rainwater desalination washing and rotary sifting, it becomes a high-performance growing substrate.
pith.p1: Water retention capacity up to 8x (800%) dry weight
pith.p2: High air-filled porosity encouraging vigorous root development
pith.p3: Verified Low-EC salinity and stable neutral pH (5.8–6.5)
pith.gain: Protects natural peat bog ecosystems and reduces commercial nursery irrigation frequency by up to 50%.

shell.name: Bio-Carbon & Briquettes
shell.imageAlt: High-calorie coconut shell charcoal briquettes beside raw polished shell
shell.description: Mature coconut shell contains dense, highly concentrated carbon. Processed through low-emission controlled pyrolysis into efficient briquettes that burn clean without deforestation.
shell.p2: Minimal ash content (<3%) with odorless, smokeless combustion
shell.p3: Burns up to 3x longer and hotter than conventional hardwood charcoal
shell.gain: Eliminates open-air agricultural burning and replaces deforestation-driven wood charcoal.

story.title: Revealing hidden value in regional agricultural wealth.
story.p1: Pandeglang Regency produces over 23,900 tons of coconuts annually across 35 districts. For decades, the husks (35% of total fruit weight) and shells (12%) were underutilized and frequently burned in open pits.
story.p2: PANDA COCO established the Keboncau Agro-Hub as a pioneering integrated processing center. Utilizing electric decorticators powered by PLN, we process 2 tons of husks monthly into certified industrial biomaterials, delivering direct value addition to farmers and local operators.

hero.title: Unlocking overlooked capital from Pandeglang coconuts.
hero.description: PANdeglang Domestic Agro COCOnut (PANDA COCO) was founded on a strategic industrial mandate: Pandeglang's 23,900-ton coconut harvest must be modernized and processed locally. Combining clean electricity and material science, we transform raw biomass into high-value manufacturing assets.
hero.imageAlt: PANDA COCO processing facility with raw coconut husks ready for electric decortication

philosophy.title: Value emerges from material science and clean technology.
philosophy.p1: A coconut husk is not worthless waste. Inside lies remarkable biological architecture: high-tensile lignin fibers, spongy cellular pith absorbing up to 8 times its weight in water, and dense endocarp shell holding 7,200 kcal/kg in carbon value.
philosophy.p2: We pair these innate biological attributes with modern electric machinery and the technical dedication of 100 trained women through OPTIMALKAN IBU. The result is a consistent, hygienic, and competitive production line engineered for modern industrial buyers.
philosophy.imageAlt: Electric decorticating machinery running smoothly at PANDA COCO Keboncau facility
philosophy.imageNote: Clean, electrified agro-biomass facility in Keboncau, Pandeglang, Banten.

vision.title: To be Indonesia's benchmark circular agro-biomass hub.
vision.description: To establish decentralized agro-industrial hubs that convert 100% of regional coconut biomass into certified circular materials, displacing petroleum-based plastics while building sustainable economic sovereignty for smallholders and rural women.

mission.title: Engineering certified biomaterials through clean technology.
mission.description: To manufacture export-grade Cocofiber, Cocopeat, Green Panels, and Bio-Briquettes via clean electric machinery, maintaining complete supply chain transparency and establishing local communities as autonomous enterprise owners.

values.title: Four pillars of manufacturing excellence.
values.lead: These benchmarks govern every stage of material extraction, laboratory validation, and commercial partnership.

v1.name: Industrial-Grade Quality
v1.text: Every batch is tested to ensure strict adherence to buyer specifications: moisture content, ash thresholds, air-filled porosity, and electrical conductivity (EC).

v2.name: Clean Electrified Production
v2.text: Replacing diesel combustion with reliable grid electricity via PLN's Electrifying Agriculture, ensuring a quiet, clean, and low-carbon processing environment.

v3.name: Sovereignty & Human Dignity
v3.text: Positioning our 60 partner farmers and 100 OPTIMALKAN IBU operators as skilled technical contributors, not charitable recipients.

v4.name: Integrity & Anti-Greenwashing
v4.text: Publishing only verified data on biomass throughput, carbon abatement, and product certifications backed by periodic field audits.

roadmap.title: Long-term vision toward a fully circular village economy.
roadmap.lead: Each phase is designed to strengthen group independence, expand machine capacity, and replicate this agro-industrial model across Pandeglang.

one.label: Phase I · Foundation & Model Validation
items: Establish the PANDA COCO Enterprise Group & OPTIMALKAN IBU vocational curriculum.
Install electric processing machinery, achieve 2 ton husk/month capacity.
Launch PANDA COCO Green Panel prototype & pilot cocopeat/cocofiber market testing.

two.label: Phase II · Standardization & Legal Formalization
items: Obtain Business Registration Number (NIB), complete laboratory quality certifications, and register trademarks.
Establish the Keboncau Circular Producer Cooperative.
Build a permanent buyer network in Banten & Jabodetabek horticultural sectors.

three.label: Phase III · Capacity Expansion & Regional Aggregation
items: Scale processing capacity to 5–10 tons/month with additional electric machine units.
Expand raw material supplier network to surrounding villages in Pandeglang.
Launch commercial production of PANDA COCO Green Panel for interior market.

four.label: Phase IV · National Penetration & Export Consortium
items: National distribution for COCOfiber, COCOpeat, and Green Panel product lines.
Collaborate with export aggregators for Asia & European markets.
Strengthen PANDA COCO Bio-Briquette export capacity for Asian culinary grilling markets.

five.label: Phase V · Replication of the Circular Agro-Hub Model
items: Transfer the electric-powered coconut processing model to other coconut-producing districts in South Banten.
Become the national reference for community-led coconut agro-biomass industrialization.

plan.label: Plan
plan.title: Monthly Production Planning
plan.text: Each month the group sets targets for husk tonnage processed, product volume, revenue, and active member count.

do.label: Do
do.title: Daily Production Logging
do.text: Every day, incoming husks, output products, and sales transactions are entered in standardized production and weighing ledgers.

check.label: Check
check.title: Monthly & Quarterly Reviews
check.text: Monthly group meetings and quarterly evaluations with PLN & Kelurahan verify achievement vs. targets and flag any quality deviations.

act.label: Act
act.title: SOP Improvement & Product Innovation
act.text: Findings drive updates to tannin-washing SOPs, labor allocation, machine maintenance schedules, or product line diversification.

supply.label: Raw Material Supply Risk
supply.text: Written agreements with transparent purchase pricing for 60 partner farmers, plus backup suppliers from surrounding villages.

quality.label: Product Quality Degradation Risk
quality.text: Desalination washing SOP, ventilated covered drying tunnels (including wet season), and moisture testing on every production batch.

wastewater.label: Tannin Wastewater Risk
wastewater.text: Tannin-bearing husk washing water is pre-settled in a sediment basin before discharge; unsold pith is composted.

safety.label: Occupational Safety (K3) Risk
safety.text: Mandatory K3 training, PPE standards, and periodic PLN-standard electrical inspections to prevent machinery and husk dust accidents.

result.title: Certified materials ready for commercial deployment.

faq.title: Answering your specification requirements.
faq.lead: We address the most frequent questions from industrial partners, commercial nurseries, and architects demanding reliable, verified biomaterial supply.

items.q: What differentiates PANDA COCOpeat from bulk market cocopeat?
items.a: PANDA COCOpeat undergoes controlled washing to reduce tannins and natural sodium chloride (Low-EC), sifted to a uniform mesh size, and maintained at an ideal pH (5.8–6.5), making it safe for direct use as a seeding medium without root-burn risk.

items.q: Is PANDA COCO Green Panel resistant to termites and tropical humidity?
items.a: Yes. Coconut coir is naturally rich in lignin (~45%), a hard biopolymer unattractive to wood-boring insects and highly resistant to decay fungi. Panels are bonded with moisture-resistant botanical binders for long-term interior durability.

items.q: How is uninterrupted raw material supply guaranteed?
items.a: We hold written supply contracts with 60 partner farmers managing 3,000 active coconut trees on a regular monthly harvest cycle (~7,000 nuts/month). Backup supply is available from surrounding coconut-producing villages in Pandeglang.

items.q: Does PANDA COCO handle custom specifications for industrial orders?
items.a: Yes. We accommodate custom cocofiber fiber length, moisture targets, panel density, and white-label retail packaging for commercial plant stores and horticultural nursery networks.

items.q: How can I schedule a field visit to the PANDA COCO Hub in Keboncau?
items.a: We warmly welcome site visits from business partners, researchers, and institutional buyers. Contact us at least 3 days in advance via our partnership form or official email to arrange a technical facility tour.
